name: E01 | Lester’s Pager Panic
summary: Filter rows where (col_A*col_B) mod col_C == 7; sort by (col_D % 2, -col_E); base-41 decode each payload via the reversed decoder; concatenate.

name: E02 | Vinewood Shift Change
summary: Pick the row whose SHA1(timestamp) ends in a3; affine-decrypt (a=7,b=11) with parameters derived from frequency_sample.bin; ignore the Caesar-5 decoy.

name: E03 | Sandy Shores Hidden Stash
summary: Carve the deleted /ledger.dat from safehouse.img, zlib-decompress, XOR every byte with the key computed from activity.log line 42's hostname (ord(3rd char) ^ ord(7th char)); decode.

name: E04 | Del Perro Camera Roll
summary: Read column-major; take 2 LSBs from R, then G, then B, MSB-first; parse a 2-byte big-endian length then a UTF-7 payload.

name: E05 | Wrong Extension, Right Exit
summary: Treat impound_dossier.pdf as ZIP; AES-128-CBC decrypt vault.enc with key=MD5(serial from the PDF form field) and IV=first 16 bytes; open vault.db; resolve delivery_hash=SHA1(plate||route); read the flag column.

name: M01 | Fleeca Vault Glitch
summary: Register a payload username, trigger the load-profile step so the stored value is interpolated into the second query, and authenticate with the custom hash sha256(pw + user[::-1] + 'GTA_SALT_v2')[:16]. Both gates must pass before the flag is returned.

name: M02 | Airport Ghost Flight
summary: Parse the classic pcap; keep frames whose magic is 0xDEAD1A70, whose CRC32 checks out and whose type is 0x0A; order by the little-endian uint32 at payload offset 6; XOR payload[10:] with the frame's CRC32 bytes; concatenate.

name: M03 | LSPD Midnight Audit
summary: Implement SHA256(prev_chain_hash + entry_data) verification; find the three forged entries at the chain breaks; apply the RLE-encoded audit_delta.bin to repair them; XOR adjacent event_code characters of the ACCEPT entries to recover the flag.

name: M04 | Underground XOR Radio
summary: XOR keystream_sample.bin with the known header from SIGNAL_SPEC.txt to obtain the keystream; run Berlekamp-Massey over GF(2) to recover the degree-23 LFSR (taps {23,5}) and its state; regenerate the full keystream; XOR it against radio_packet.bin.

name: M05 | Debugging the Dispatch
summary: Guard the shared counter with a lock; the fixed dispatcher emits a base85+zlib JSON blob containing stage2.py; correct stage2's checksum so it masks to 32 bits explicitly; its output is the flag.

name: H01 | Zancudo Deadbolt
summary: Defeat both anti-debug traps; locate the .data vault (a unique 256-byte permutation of 0..255 preceded by a u32 length); per byte compute r = TARGET[i] * K[i]^-1 mod 251 and invert the S-box; the recovered string is the flag.

name: H02 | The Recursive Freeway
summary: Pre-filter candidate nodes by degree sequence and clustering coefficient; find the unique induced 12-node subgraph isomorphic to template.json; verify it via the ordered Laplacian eigenvalue fingerprint; build the flag from the subgraph's node labels per PROTOCOL.md.

name: H03 | Impound Evidence Matryoshka
summary: LSB column-major 2-bit extraction, then AES-256-CTR (PBKDF2 key from the metadata-derived passphrase), then an MTX-1 matrix code, then a Huffman decode using the tree from EVIDENCE_NOTE.txt, then run the recovered Python stage, which deterministically prints the flag.

name: H04 | LEGAL RAGGING
summary: Call sign_debug on a fixed message to obtain one correct and one faulty signature; p = gcd(bad^e - m mod n, n); q = n//p; d = inv(e,(p-1)(q-1)); sign ADMIN_MESSAGE; submit the token; the gateway returns the flag held in the FTA_H04_FLAG environment variable.

name: H05 | Last Ride Out
summary: Parse the TLV transcript; identify the three parties; recognise that party C's key material is accepted unauthenticated; substitute an attacker-known C share so the effective session key equals a known value; AES-GCM decrypt final_payload.enc using the prepended 96-bit nonce.
